name: Roppen
kurzbeschreibung: Lively community in the Oberinntal between Imst and Haiming, featuring a charming lakeside bath and an extensive cycling network.
text:
Überblick

Roppen is situated in the Tyrolean Upper Inn Valley within the Imst district at an elevation of 724 metres, nestled where the rushing Ötztaler Ache river flows into the Inn River, home to around 1,920 residents. The municipality spans a sunny alluvial terrace at the foot of the imposing Tschirgant mountain (2,370 m). Roppen presents an extraordinary contrast: serene rural traditions and natural geological wonders like its bizarre earth pyramids meet world-class adrenaline sports, with the world-famous AREA 47 adventure park situated within its municipal borders at the gateway to the Ötztal valley.

Geschichte

Roppen was first documented in 1260 as Roupen, derived from the Latin word for steep cliffs, denoting the precipitous rock walls of the Tschirgant. Archaeological findings confirm Bronze Age settlements dating back over 3,000 years. From medieval times through the 18th century, active silver, lead, and zinc mines dotted the slopes. A unique geological phenomenon are the Roppen Earth Pyramids in the Walderbach valley: melting glaciers left moraine silt 10,000 years ago, which torrential rain eroded away around protective boulders, sculpting fragile stone pillars up to eight metres tall. An essential wooden bridge across the Inn was recorded as early as 1456. The mineral spring at Römerbadl continues to supply pure water to local Kneipp baths. The parish church of Saint Leonard was erected between 1853 and 1860 in neoclassical Romanesque revival style.

Anreise

Roppen boasts exceptional transport infrastructure. Motorists travel via the Inntalautobahn A12, using the Ötztal exit directly beside AREA 47 or the Imst-Ost exit, while the B171 Tiroler Straße passes directly through the village. The 5.1-kilometre Roppen Tunnel diverts expressway transit. Rail passengers arrive at Roppen station along the Arlberg railway, served hourly by S-Bahn Tirol trains (lines S4 and S5). The international express rail hub Ötztal-Bahnhof lies only four kilometres to the east.

Tipps

The premier global magnet for outdoor action is AREA 47, featuring a 20,000-square-metre Water AREA with extreme waterslides, a 27-metre diving tower, cable wakeboarding, and Austria's highest aerial ropes course. Nature lovers will enjoy the family-friendly hiking circuit up to the Roppen Earth Pyramids in Hohenegg, featuring secured viewing platforms. Cyclists can follow the flat Inn-Radweg trail along the riverbank, stopping for revitalizing dips at the Römerbadl Kneipp spring. Climbers can explore high-grade granite sport climbing routes nearby at Tumpen and the Engelswand crags.
